# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

I read this score from the code. Every applicable rule is clear. The one thing the code can't show is whether a CDN or firewall in front of the site lets real crawlers through.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is wrong, so there are no fixes to do first. The biggest unknown is bot protection, because code can't show it.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your hosting
- **Why it matters:** A CDN or firewall can block crawlers even when `robots.txt` allows them.
- **Where:** outside the repository, in your hosting or CDN settings.
- **What the code says:** `Allow: /` (`public/robots.txt:2`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100 whether it comes back clear or a problem, because this isn't a scored rule. It tells you whether the code score reflects what crawlers actually get.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain text with valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says they should | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Only `*` is allowed, and `/account` is the only block. Policy is `allow`. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 sampled routes have no noindex. `app/account/page.tsx:1` is noindex on purpose and isn't in the sitemap. |
| GEO-015 | Canonical is absolute and on your own domain | Clear | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1` and `app/visit/page.tsx:1` each have their own absolute canonical on `www.orchard.example` |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in server HTML | Clear | Server Components in the Next.js app router, with no client fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | A sitemap exists and is discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, and `public/robots.txt:11` has the absolute `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` are present | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:5` sets `lang="en"`, and all 3 public pages have a title and description |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:7` has `<a href>` links to all three public pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with the AI-search policy | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:9` uses `data-nosnippet` on one element only, and there is no page-wide nosnippet |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | I read `app/layout.tsx` and the 4 pages. There are no images, and the nav links have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | No `llms.txt` exists. This is never scored. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not an app. This is never scored. |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Label the business with structured data:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` Add Organization or LocalBusiness JSON-LD with the name, location and a link to the site. Nothing states the site's identity in a machine-readable way yet.
- **Say when and where in text on /visit:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'` The page promises directions but only has `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Add the address, the hours and how to get there as text, and mark them up as LocalBusiness `openingHoursSpecification` and `address`.
- **Give each variety its own page:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` The page claims forty varieties but names only two. Pages such as `/varieties/ashmeads-kernel` would each get their own address, and you could list them on the index page.
- **Add `lastmod` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. If you know when pages last changed, adding `<lastmod>` might help crawlers decide when to revisit.
- **Add social tags:** `app/layout.tsx:1`: `export const metadata = { metadataBase: ... }`. No `openGraph` title, description or image is set, so link previews have little to show.
- **Add a viewport and canonical to every page:** `app/account/page.tsx:1` has no description. That's fine for a private page. For the public pages, the Next.js metadata API already supplies the charset and viewport.
- **Link between related pages:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4` and `app/varieties/page.tsx:4` have no onward links in their content. A link from varieties to visit (for example, "see them in the orchard") would help readers and crawlers move between related pages.
- **Make titles say who and where:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Apple varieties'` and `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Visit the orchard'`. These don't name the orchard or Herefordshire. Something like "Apple varieties | Orchard, Herefordshire" says more about the page.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status and headers:** real status codes, redirects and `X-Robots-Tag` headers can't be read from the code. A live scan would confirm them.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- Blocking `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` (`public/robots.txt:5-9`) is a deliberate training-crawler choice, so I didn't count it. It matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"`.
- The noindex and `/account` block on the account page are deliberate.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
